nimijātaka: [Nimi+jātaka]  CL=7 The life story of King Nimi, who was a Bodhisatta, is known as the Nimijātaka. He was the last king of the Maghadeva dynasty and greatly delighted in dāna (generosity) and sīla (moral conduct). Due to his wholesome deeds, he traveled to observe the hell realm and the deva realm aboard the Vejayantā chariot sent by Sakka. He then preached about the suffering in the hell realm and the happiness in the deva realm. One day, he saw one of his hairs turn white. At that moment, he was filled with remorse and contrition and chose to become a monk.

nimittabyākaraṇīya: [Nimitta+byāka+raṇīya]  CL=7 A thera named Nimittabyākaraṇīya, renowned as a foreteller, lived near the Himavantā mountain in ancient times. He taught the skill of the Vedas to 54,000 disciples. During that era, a Bodhisatta named Tisā passed away in the Tusitā Deva realm and took conception in the human realm. At that very moment, an earthquake occurred, prompting many people to approach Venerable Nimittabyākaraṇīya to inquire about its cause. The venerable foretold that a Lord Buddha would soon enlighten the world. He then guided the people to observe the five precepts. Due to this meritorious deed, Venerable Nimittabyākaraṇīya did not fall into the lower realms for 92 world cycles. Eventually, in the era of Buddha Tisā, he attained Arahantship with the Paṭisambhidāñāṇa (analytical knowledge). See -  spa, 2. 45.

nimittasaññaka: [Nimitta+saññaka]  CL=7 A thera named Nimittasaññaka, who developed Buddhānussati nimittasaññā. This thera, previously a hermit, lived near the Candabhāga River in a monastery. One day, while wandering in the forest, he saw a golden deer grazing. His mind became purified upon seeing the deer, and he developed the Buddhānussati saññā, reflecting on the Lord Buddhas—those who are enlightened, enlightening, and destined to enlighten—comparing their gracefulness to that golden deer. As a result of this meritorious deed, he avoided the lower realms for 94 eons. In one of those lifetimes, he became a universal monarch named Araññasattha in the 27th world from this Bhadda world. Later, in the present era of Gotama Buddha, he was reborn as the venerable Nimittasaññaka Thera. He attained the four aspects of paṭisambhidā, the eight attainments (samāpatti), and the six supernormal knowledges (abhiññā). He dedicated himself to spreading the teachings of Lord Buddha.

nimittasutta: [Nimitta+sutta]  CL=1 The Nimitta Sutta explains offenses using the simile of a goldsmith. It describes how a bhikkhu who practices the noble methods of samatha and vipassanā sometimes focuses on samādhi (concentration), sometimes on vīriya (effort), and sometimes on upekkhā (equanimity). By balancing these three causes equally in his meditation, he avoids the offenses that might arise, just as a goldsmith carefully tempers gold to achieve perfection.

nimokkhasutta: [Nimokkha+sutta]  CL=7 The discourse in the Nimokkha Sutta relates to a question posed by the deva Rūpāvacara Brahmā to the Buddha: 'Why do you know the reasons for the nimokkha (path to liberation), pamokkha (fruit of emancipation), and viveka (detachment or Nibbāna) for living beings?'
